root_cause.text: KCOV instrumentation was allowed to run in x86 kexec code after load_segments() changed segment registers and invalidated the GS base, so KCOV’s per-CPU data access in subsequent instrumented functions crashed the kernel.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states that “load_segments() function changes segment registers, invalidating GS base (which KCOV relies on for per-cpu data)” and that “any subsequent instrumented C code call (e.g. native_gdt_invalidate()) begins crashing the kernel in an endless loop,” and the fix disables KCOV for machine_kexec_64.o and physaddr.o.

intent_record.intent_summary: Disable KCOV instrumentation for `machine_kexec_64.o` to prevent kexec-time crashes caused by GS base invalidation.
intent_record.what: A new makefile entry, `KCOV_INSTRUMENT_machine_kexec_64.o := n`, was added along with explanatory comments stating that KCOV instrumentation is disabled for the entire `machine_kexec_64.o` source file due to kexec-related GS base invalidation.
intent_record.how: This prevents the build system from applying KCOV instrumentation to `machine_kexec_64.o`, avoiding runtime crashes during kexec paths where `load_segments()` invalidates the GS base that KCOV uses for per-CPU data, while leaving KCOV enabled elsewhere in the kernel.

intent_record.intent_summary: Disable KCOV instrumentation for physaddr.o to avoid unsafe or unsupported coverage instrumentation in that low-level x86 object.
intent_record.what: A new makefile assignment was added to disable KCOV instrumentation for physaddr.o by setting KCOV_INSTRUMENT_physaddr.o := n, along with a comment referencing the existing "Disable KCOV" comment in arch/x86/kernel/Makefile.
intent_record.how: This prevents the physaddr.o object from being built with KCOV coverage instrumentation, avoiding KCOV-related code generation for that file at runtime and build time, likely to keep it compatible with low-level execution constraints similar to other excluded x86 memory-related objects.
